points.description: States that a queue is a data structure that stores elements in first in, first out (FIFO) order, so the first element added is the first one removed.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for saying it is a data structure or collection that holds elements in some order, without stating FIFO or first-in-first-out.

points.description: Names enqueue and dequeue as the main operations of a queue (enqueue to add an element, dequeue to remove one).
points.partial_credit: Half mark for naming only one of the two operations, or naming them without saying what they do.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) require the FIFO principle stated for the queue as a data structure, plus both operations enqueue and dequeue named. Answers that give FIFO but omit the operations get 4, and answers that name enqueue and dequeue but not FIFO get at most 1, with part marks as described. Answers that only describe a queue vaguely (for example, a line of people with no order principle) or describe a different structure such as a stack (LIFO) earn no marks for P1; extra correct detail is fine.
